newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open mostly firmer ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open mostly firmer ahead of auction.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer on Tuesday ahead of today's weekly T-bill tender with some overseas and account buying helping boost prices slightly, dealers said.

"Maybe the market felt we had backed up enough yesterday and was getting a little bit of confidence that the currency was settling out," said one T-bill trader with a bank-owned brokerage. "I'm a little surprised we've held in this well on the day of an auction."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.36 percent from 3.38 percent at Monday's close.

Canadian T-bills have softened for several of the past few sessions as weakness in the Canadian dollar increased speculation that the Bank of Canada would hike interest rates for a second time this year.
However, the Canadian dollar opened little changed on Tuesday at C$1.3847 (US$0.721) after Monday's close of C$1.3849 (US$0.7220).
Dealers are now looking ahead to the auction of C$4.6 billion three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills. Results of the auction will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.76 percent from 3.78 percent at Monday's close. The one-year when-issued T-bill traded unchanged to yield 4.28 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.25 percent, in the middle of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
